kunyah: Abu Umara — Asad Allah, the Lion of Allah
era: The Lion of Allah — Martyr of Uhud
teaser: He split Abu Jahl's head open before he had ever prayed. At Uhud he fought with a sword in each hand.
quran_mention: The ayah that came down while the Prophet ﷺ stood over his body: «وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُم بِهِ» — 'And if you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what you were afflicted with.' (16:126)

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: Uncle by blood, brother by the same milk
layers.content:
Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim — the Prophet's paternal uncle, and only four years older than him. His mother was Hala bint Uhayb of Zuhra. His kunya was Abu Umara. Ibn Sa'd heads his entry with the title the community gave him: the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger.

The relationship was closer than the family tree shows. Years later Ali suggested the Prophet ﷺ marry Hamzah's daughter, calling her the most beautiful girl in Quraysh. The answer settled it: 'Ali, do you not know that Hamzah was my brother by suckling, and that Allah has forbidden through suckling what He has forbidden through lineage?' The two of them had been nursed by the same woman. They grew up in the same clan, close in age, in a household where the boy who would be sent had no father.

He was a man of medium height. He fathered Ya'la, Amir, Umara and Umama, and Ibn Sa'd notes plainly what happened to that line: Ya'la's sons all died, and no descendants of Hamzah remain. His daughter Umama was later the subject of a custody dispute among Ali, Ja'far and Zayd ibn Harithah, each of whom wanted her.
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Hamzah was my brother by suckling, and what is forbidden by suckling is what is forbidden by lineage' — narrated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: He came in furious and left a Muslim
layers.content:
Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi told it simply. One day Abu Jahl, Adi ibn al-Hamra and Ibn al-Asda set on the Prophet ﷺ in public, abusing and insulting him. Hamzah heard about it. He walked into the mosque in a rage and struck Abu Jahl across the head with a blow that opened his skull.

Then — in Ibn Sa'd's sequence, immediately after — Hamzah became Muslim, and the Messenger of Allah was made strong through him. It was after the Prophet ﷺ had begun teaching in the house of al-Arqam, in the sixth year of the mission.

So his Islam did not begin with a verse or an argument. It began with family loyalty and a temper, and then it became something else entirely. What he had defended out of blood he now believed.

And he pushed at it. Hamzah asked the Prophet ﷺ to show him Jibril as he actually is. 'You will not be able to see him.' 'Yes I will.' 'Then sit where you are.' Jibril came down on the wooden rack in the Ka'bah where the idolaters hung their clothes while making tawaf. 'Raise your eyes and look.' Hamzah looked. The narration says Jibril's feet were like emeralds, and the bravest man in Makkah fell down unconscious.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (reports of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Ammar ibn Abu Ammar)

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: The first banner of Islam was put in his hand
layers.content:
Ibn Sa'd states it as the position his teachers settled on: the first banner the Messenger of Allah ever handed to anyone was given to Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib. It was for a patrol of thirty riders down along the coast to meet a Qurayshi caravan coming up from Syria. Abu Jahl was in that caravan with three hundred riders. The two forces passed each other without a blow being struck.

He carried the banner again at Banu Qaynuqa, on a day when no other standards were raised. At Badr he wore an ostrich feather so he could be identified in the fighting, and one narration from Ali has the Prophet ﷺ saying in the middle of that battle, 'Ali, call Hamzah for me' — because Hamzah was the man nearest to the enemy line.

When the brotherhood pairs were made in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ joined Hamzah with Zayd ibn Harithah, a former slave, and Hamzah took it seriously enough that on the morning of Uhud he named Zayd the executor of his estate before he went out to fight.

That is worth sitting with. The uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, of Banu Hashim, put his family's affairs in the hands of a man who had been bought and sold.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (reports of Yazid ibn Ruman and Ali ibn Abi Talib)

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: Two swords at Uhud, and what was done afterwards
layers.content:
Umayr ibn Ishaq described him at Uhud fighting with a sword in each hand, out in front of the Prophet ﷺ, moving forward and back and calling out, 'I am the lion of Allah.' Then he stumbled and went down on his back, and Wahshi ibn Harb, who had been watching for him, threw a spear and split him open. He was fifty-nine. Uhud came thirty-two months after the Hijrah.

What happened next is why his name carries what it carries. Hind bint Utba had vowed that if she reached Hamzah she would eat from his liver. His body was cut open and mutilated; she was brought a piece of it, chewed it, and could not swallow. When the Prophet ﷺ was told, he said that Allah had forbidden the Fire ever to taste the flesh of Hamzah.

He went and stood over his uncle and could not bear to look. Abu Hurayrah's narration keeps his words: 'You were what you know — keeping ties of kinship and doing good.' In grief he swore he would mutilate seventy of them in Hamzah's place. Jibril came down while he was still standing there with the end of Surah an-Nahl: if you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what was done to you. He made expiation for the oath, and did not do it, and was patient.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 16:126 — 'And if you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what you were afflicted with'
layers.hadith_ref: The Prophet ﷺ said of Hamzah: 'Allah has forbidden the Fire to ever taste the flesh of Hamzah' — Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The cloth was too short, and the ummah never forgot
layers.content:
His sister Safiyya came onto the field looking for him. Ali and az-Zubayr tried to keep it from her. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'I fear for her mind,' put his hand on her chest and prayed. She said, 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return,' and wept. She had brought two cloths to shroud her brother. There was an Ansari lying dead beside him, so Hamzah was wrapped in the wider one and the Ansari in the other.

Even then it did not reach. Khabbab's report: when they covered his head his feet came out, and when they covered his feet his head came out. The Prophet ﷺ said to cover his face, and had the idhkhir plant laid over his feet. The companions standing at the grave were weeping. Asked why, they said they could not find a garment that day fit for his uncle.

He was the first martyr the Prophet ﷺ prayed over at Uhud, and then the other dead were brought and laid beside him group after group so that he was prayed over again with each of them. When the Prophet ﷺ remarked that there were no women weeping for Hamzah, the Ansar sent theirs. From that day, it is said, no woman of the Ansar mourned her own dead without weeping for Hamzah first. Fatimah used to go and tend his grave.
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley (reports of Khabbab, Abu Usayd as-Sa'idi, Ibn Abbas)

quiz.prompt: What was the relationship between Hamzah and the Prophet ﷺ beyond being his uncle?

options.text: They were also cousins through their mothers
They were foster brothers, nursed by the same woman
Hamzah had been his guardian after Abu Talib
Hamzah was married to one of his daughters

quiz.citation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas and by Ali — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: It came out when Ali proposed that the Prophet ﷺ marry Hamzah's daughter. He answered that what is forbidden by suckling is forbidden as if by lineage — so she was his niece twice over.

quiz.prompt: What immediately preceded Hamzah's acceptance of Islam?

options.text: He heard Surah Taha recited at the Ka'bah
He struck Abu Jahl's head open for insulting the Prophet ﷺ
A dream in which he saw his father
Abu Bakr spoke to him privately about it

quiz.citation: Narrated by Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: It began as clan loyalty and a temper, in the sixth year of the mission. Ibn Sa'd's next sentence is that Hamzah became Muslim and the Messenger of Allah was made strong through him.

quiz.prompt: What did Ibn Sa'd's teachers agree was the first banner the Prophet ﷺ ever handed out?

options.text: The banner at Badr, given to Ali
The banner at Khaybar, given to Umar
A coastal patrol of thirty riders, given to Hamzah
The banner of Banu Qaynuqa, given to Mus'ab ibn Umayr

quiz.citation: Narrated by Yazid ibn Ruman; Ibn Sa'd states this is the report agreed upon — Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Thirty riders went out to meet a Qurayshi caravan escorted by three hundred, with Abu Jahl among them. The two forces passed without fighting.

quiz.prompt: Whom did Hamzah appoint as executor of his estate on the morning of Uhud?

options.text: Ali ibn Abi Talib
Zayd ibn Harithah, his brother in the pairing made by the Prophet ﷺ
His sister Safiyya
az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam

quiz.citation: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III — reported by Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar
quiz.scholar_reflection: An uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, of Banu Hashim, handed his family's affairs to a man who had once been bought and sold. The brotherhood was not a ceremony.

quiz.prompt: What happened when the Prophet ﷺ swore, over Hamzah's body, that he would mutilate seventy of the enemy?

options.text: Abu Bakr persuaded him against it
Jibril came down with the end of Surah an-Nahl, and he made expiation for the oath instead
He carried it out at the Battle of the Trench
He asked the companions to decide

quiz.citation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III; Quran 16:126
quiz.scholar_reflection: The ayah set a ceiling on retaliation at the exact moment the grief was highest. He paid the expiation for the oath, did not do it, and was patient.

quiz.prompt: Hamzah's faith started as loyalty to family before it became conviction. Where do your good actions actually start from?

options.text: Duty to people I love, and belief catches up later
Conviction first — I need to be persuaded
Habit, mostly, and I do not examine it
Anger at something unjust, more often than I would like

quiz.citation: Reflection on the account of Hamzah's Islam, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He walked into that mosque for his nephew, not for a doctrine. Allah takes people in through the door they happen to be standing at.

quiz.prompt: He insisted on seeing Jibril as he really is, and collapsed. What do you do at the edge of what you can handle?

options.text: I push, and sometimes I pay for it
I stop early and call it wisdom
I want to know the limit even if it costs me
I avoid finding out where the edge is

quiz.citation: Narrated by Ammar ibn Abu Ammar — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He was warned he would not be able to bear it and asked anyway. There is no rebuke in the narration — only the fact that the bravest man in Makkah went down.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet ﷺ was given a limit on revenge at the worst moment of his grief. What holds you back when you have been genuinely wronged?

options.text: A rule I hold, even when I do not feel it
Fear of the consequences more than principle
Nothing, in the moment — only later regret
Someone else talking me down

quiz.citation: Reflection on Quran 16:126 and the narration of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Sa'd Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The verse did not forbid response. It capped it at what was done to you. That is a harder discipline than being told simply to forgive.

quiz.prompt: Safiyya brought two cloths for her brother and gave one to a stranger lying beside him. What does grief make you capable of?

options.text: It closes me in on my own loss
It makes me notice other people's losses more
It depends whether anyone is helping me
I have not been tested by real grief yet

quiz.citation: Narrated by Hisham ibn Urwa — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: She had come to bury her brother and had exactly two cloths. She kept the wider one for him and left with none for herself.

quiz.prompt: The companions wept because they could not find a shroud long enough for the Prophet's uncle. What does that tell you about the early ummah?

options.text: That honour was never about what they could provide
That they carried real shame at what they could not give
That the community's poverty was not a metaphor
All three, and the tears were all of them at once

quiz.citation: Narrated by Abu Usayd as-Sa'idi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The cloth covered his head or his feet, not both. That detail survived fourteen centuries because the people standing there could not stop looking at it.
